title: The OpenAPI contract is the only reference for the current HTTP API
requirement: Register decision DR-Q7 (2026-09-27); REST API Specification §2.2 principle 2 (OpenAPI is the source of truth) and §19 item 4 (required scopes declared for every operation); register tasks DR-B2, DR-B3, DR-D1
acceptance: Every protected OpenAPI operation declares security [{mutualTls: [scope]}] where scope is what AuthorizationPolicyEngine.requiredScope enforces for that route
Exactly the paths in PublicEndpoints are declared with security: []
components.schemas.AgentStatus lists the values the server writes (AgentStatus.getValue())
POST /api/v1/transfers and POST /api/v1/service-connections/{serviceConnectionId}/validate declare 409, 503 and 504 problem responses (ControllerConnectionAuthorizer)
The getApiInfo response schema declares openApi and no endpoint inventory
GET /api/v1/info returns openApi = /api/v1/openapi.yaml and no endpoints field
The REST API Specification rows marked Current are exactly the declared operations, with parameter names normalised
classification: contract (OpenAPI document against the policy engine, the core enum and the specification) and external-path behavioral (GET /api/v1/info over HTTP)

preparatoryRefactor.change: The public-path rule was duplicated as a private isPublic method in AuthenticationHandler and AuthorizationHandler. It was extracted to PublicEndpoints, used by both, so that the contract test can check the OpenAPI public operations against the same definition. Behaviour-preserving.

red.revision: 2b93940 plus the preparatory refactor and the new tests
red.result: 21 tests, 6 failures, each for the intended missing behaviour: 49 operations without a declared scope; AgentStatus enum [REGISTERED, ONLINE, BUSY, OFFLINE, UNHEALTHY, DRAINING, DEREGISTERED] against the server values [registering, healthy, ...]; no 504 on POST /api/v1/transfers; getApiInfo schema without openApi; GET /api/v1/info returning no openApi; GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml not marked Current in the specification. The guard test onlyThePublicEndpointsAreDeclaredWithoutSecurity passed, as intended.

green.change: InfoHandler returns openApi instead of a hand-written endpoint list. The OpenAPI contract declares the scope of each of the 49 protected operations (taken from the scopes the policy engine reported in the red log), the server's agent statuses, the DNS-authorization failure responses and a typed getApiInfo schema. The specification lists GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml as Current.

mutations: DELETE /api/v1/transfers/{jobId} declares transfers:read instead of transfers:delete
The specification marks GET /api/v1/agents as Required instead of Current
mutationCheck.result: Both detected: everyOperationDeclaresTheScopeThePolicyEngineEnforces and restSpecificationCurrentRowsMatchTheContract failed naming the mutated operation. Files restored from copies afterwards.

refactor: Test assertions tidied (assertFalse). Documentation, not behaviour: the OpenAPI contract gained the descriptions the API Reference carried (current transfer events, agent report atomicity and idempotent resends, preparation failures, probe semantics and default ports, partial-update trust retention, security-event paging and retention, FTPS ports, DNS failure responses) and declares the Service Connections and Security Events tags. The REST API Specification v2.6 is requirements only. QUORUS_API_REFERENCE.md is deleted and its seven live links repointed to the contract.
replacedTests: HttpApiServerHealthTest.shouldIncludeAllEndpointCategories and shouldListExpectedEndpointCounts asserted the hand-written endpoint list in /api/v1/info, which is removed. The route inventory they approximated is enforced by OpenApiContractTest against the registered routes.

regression.result: per-module totals (core, workflow, tenant, controller, agent): 1575 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; 134 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; 64 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; 574 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; 101 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped

limitations: Only the two operations known to call ControllerConnectionAuthorizer are checked for 409/503/504; the test names them explicitly because the call graph is not derived.
The descriptive text moved into the contract is not machine-checked beyond parsing.
CI has never passed (ENG-07, deferred by SEQ-01); this slice's regression evidence is the local run above.
sensitiveDataCheck: Logs contain Maven and test output only; no request bodies, credentials, keys or sensitive payloads.
